subject.name: Ocean Bottle
subject.selection: Retained as the task’s startup website subject because an active direct-to-consumer website is publicly accessible. The 2019 founding-year statement supplied in the task authorization was not independently verified in this collection, so the report does not state it as a fact.

observations.observed: Canonical homepage; title ‘The World's Most Needed Reusable Water Bottle’; description and H1 frame reusable bottles and ocean-plastic collection; navigation links to collections, product pages, impact, FAQs, contact, and news.
Canonical product page; title ‘Ocean Bottle Original | Insulated Reusable Water Bottle’; product H1 ‘Original Bottle’; delivered markup links to related products, FAQs, and the impact page.

Canonical FAQ page; title ‘FAQs | Ocean Bottle’; H1 ‘Frequently Asked Questions’; visible section headings cover plastic collection, returns, delivery, warranty, pre-orders, product, engraving, and discounts.

Canonical impact page; title and description make Ocean Bottle’s plastic-collection statement; H1 ‘Our Impact’; headings include ‘1 for 1000’, ‘How it works’, partners, and a company statement about B Corp certification.
B Lab directory could not be retrieved from this cloud environment; it is not used to validate certification.

measurement: Use consent-aware analytics and a documented UTM taxonomy: source, medium, campaign, content, term.
Keep paid-platform reporting separate from analytics attribution; reconcile purchase events only after consent and implementation review.
Define CAC as media spend divided by attributed new customers; define ROAS as attributed revenue divided by media spend. Zero denominators produce an explicit unavailable result.
